data.title: Viral BTS row between Thai woman and noisy tourists sparks online debate
data.description: A heated confrontation between a Thai woman and a group of foreign teenage tourists aboard a Bangkok BTS Skytrain on Friday has gone viral, triggering widespread debate on social media over public behaviour and cultural respect.

data.title: Narathiwat taps into martial law measures after deadly ranger attack
data.description: NARATHIWAT - Stricter security measures allowed under martial law have been imposed across Narathiwat amid efforts to track down militants responsible for an attack that killed five paramilitary rangers earlier in the week.

data.title: Phuket prepares for weekend downpours
data.description: PHUKET - Up to ten large pumps have been installed around municipal Phuket in preparation to deal with the possibility of more flooding after rains inundated several areas earlier on Friday.

data.title: 12 Chinese nationals arrested in Tak
data.description: Twelve Chinese nationals were arrested after allegedly crossing illegally into Thailand from Myanmar and attempting to hide in a cornfield in the Mae Sot district of Tak province.

data.title: Thailand passport ranking slides, 5th in Asean
data.description: The Thai passport went slightly down in the global ranking this year, as Singapore still underlined its most powerful travel document in the ratings.

data.title: Thailand to crack down on Myanmar's Jalobo network
data.description: Thai authorities are preparing a major operation against suspected drug traffickers linked to Myanmar drug kingpin Col Jalobo while seeking the return of a key suspect accused of recruiting a Thai Airways cabin crew member arrested in Australia for carrying heroin.

data.title: Govt keen to start UK FTA talks
data.description: Thailand is seeking to strengthen trade and investment ties with the United Kingdom.

data.title: Govt to crack down on Jalobo's network
data.description: Thai authorities are preparing a major operation against suspected drug traffickers linked to Myanmar drug kingpin Colonel Jalobo while seeking the return of a key suspect accused of recruiting a Thai Airways cabin crew member arrested in Australia for carrying heroin.

data.title: Anutin orders new anti-graft push
data.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has ordered a broader anti-corruption push, with new measures targeting bribery risks, unclear government procedures and fraud in public recruitment.

data.title: Balancing act on Myanmar
data.description: Thailand is walking a diplomatic tightrope as it seeks to facilitate efforts to address the Myanmar crisis. On July 12-13, Thailand hosted informal Asean meetings in Bangkok and Pattaya, bringing together Asean foreign ministers, Myanmar's foreign minister, the National Solidarity and Peacemaking Negotiation Committee (NSPNC) and six ethnic armed organisations (EAOs).

data.title: Ministry to revamp civil service exams
data.description: The Interior Ministry has pledged to overhaul recruitment procedures for local civil servants by requiring examination scores to be announced immediately after tests, following a major exam-rigging scandal affecting thousands of candidates.

data.title: PM defends stance on China
data.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul dismissed Taiwan's criticism of Thailand's support for the One China policy on Thursday, saying Bangkok's position would not affect economic ties with Taipei.

data.title: LGBTQ+ economy seen as growth engine
data.description: Thailand should recognise its LGBTQ+ economy as a new growth engine that requires legal and structural reforms to attract investment and enhance global competitiveness, according to several speakers.

data.title: 17.3m workers 'unable to support their retirement'
data.description: Thailand's ageing population is raising concerns over retirement security, with 17.3 million "near-retirement" workers facing a high risk of insufficient savings to support them in old age, according to the National Savings Fund (NSF).

data.title: Anutin stands firm on iLaw suit over poll claims
data.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has insisted he will not withdraw a defamation lawsuit against iLaw director Yingcheep Atchanont over allegations linked to the 2024 Senate election, saying legal action is the right of those affected.

data.title: Welfare card rules rejigged
data.description: The Finance Ministry has revised the eligibility criteria for the state welfare card scheme, allowing owners of older vehicles to retain their benefits while extending the deadline for unsuccessful applicants to appeal until Sept 20.

data.title: AI crocodile sparks school search in Chon Buri
data.description: CHON BURI: A photograph appearing to show a crocodile lurking in floodwater at a school in Sattahip district sparked a frantic search on Thursday involving rescue workers, police and local officials, only for a student to later admit he had created the image using artificial intelligence.

data.title: Bitcoin miners ‘stole power worth B280 million’
data.description: The Department of Special Investigation has seized about 1,900 cryptocurrency mining machines after uncovering large-scale electricity theft estimated at 280 million baht linked to illegal bitcoin mining in Samut Sakhon.

data.title: PP attacks changes to welfare card terms
data.description: The People's Party (PP) has criticised the government's revised state welfare card criteria, saying the changes reflect poor policy coordination and could exclude vulnerable people from assistance.
